native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB: From 1985 onwards, the median Family net wealth of the Non-Black Non-Hispanic cohort (cohort==3, used here as a ~White proxy because the codebook does not isolate non-Hispanic Whites) is substantially higher than that of the Black (cohort==1) and Hispanic (cohort==2) cohorts in NLSY79, in every wealth snapshot available in the file (1985, 1990, 1996) and in both per-year available-case and balanced sub-sample analyses. In nominal dollars, 1996 medians are $42,600 (White-proxy, n=3,557) vs $9,800 (Black, n=1,368) vs $2,562.5 (Hispanic, n=2,114); in 1996 the median Black household holds ~23% and the median Hispanic household ~6% of the median White-proxy household's wealth. The cohort rank-ordering ~White-proxy > Black > Hispanic and the widening absolute and relative gap are robust to attrition handling. Caveats: cohort==3 is only an approximation to White (it also includes Asians, Native Americans, and mixed/other respondents); there is no sampling-weight variable in data/nls_raw.csv so all medians are unweighted; figures are family-level nominal dollars; only the three supplied waves (1985, 1990, 1996) are reported; no CPI deflation, no winsorization, top-coding, or log-transform applied to the headline.

Restrict to respondents with non-null wealth in 1985, 1990 and 1996 (balanced sample, n=5,739) and recompute medians (robustness). Compute ancillary component medians (residential property, farm/business/other, vehicles, items>$500) at 1996 only. Compute 1996 Black/White-proxy and Hispanic/White-proxy ratios for both panels.
